highlights.title: Overview
highlights.value:
Founded in 1865 by industrialist Asa Packer, Lehigh University is a premier private research university located in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. It is recognized as an R1 institution, representing the highest level of research activity in the United States. You will find that Lehigh perfectly balances the resources of a powerful research university with the personal atmosphere of a small college.

The university is organized into five prestigious colleges:

  • College of Arts and Sciences
  • College of Business
  • College of Health
  • College of Education
  • P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science

highlights.title: Student life
highlights.value:
At Lehigh, your life outside the classroom will be just as vibrant as your studies. You can join a diverse community represented by students from over 40 countries. With numerous student-run organizations like the Mustard & Cheese Drama Society, the Marching 97, and the Lehigh Coffee Club, there is truly something for everyone.

The university also provides robust support services, including academic advising and health resources like Peer Health Advisors, ensuring you feel supported throughout your journey.

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
You have several housing options that make living on campus both convenient and engaging. The Asa Packer Campus hosts several residence halls and complexes, such as the Centennial Complex, Brodhead House, and Sayre Park. These spaces are designed to foster community and provide easy access to academic buildings.

If you are looking for budget-friendly accommodation options outside the campus, feel free to download our app and check out the Stays feature!

highlights.title: Facilities
highlights.value:
1. Library

You will have access to world-class resources at Lehigh's libraries. The Linderman Library, famous for its stunning Victorian Rotunda, houses humanities and social sciences collections. Meanwhile, the Fairchild-Martindale Library (FML) focuses on science, engineering, and business, offering modern study spaces and digital resources.

2. Sports

Lehigh’s "Mountain Hawks" have access to top-tier athletic facilities on the Murray H. Goodman Campus. This includes the Stabler Arena, Murray H. Goodman Stadium, and the Taylor Gymnasium, which features fitness centres and training spaces for both varsity athletes and recreational use.

3. Laboratories

As a research-intensive school, Lehigh offers specialized labs across its campuses. Notable facilities include the Fritz Engineering Laboratory, the Imbt Laboratories, and the Sinclair Laboratory. The recently opened Health, Science and Technology (HST) Building provides state-of-the-art integrated research spaces.

4. Cafeteria

You won't go hungry with the variety of dining options available. Popular spots include Rathbone Hall, which offers a traditional dining experience with great views, and Lamberton Hall. You can also find quick bites and coffee at various kiosks and cafes across the campuses.

highlights.title: Campuses
highlights.value:
Asa Packer Campus

This is the historic heart of the university, located on the slopes of South Mountain. It houses most of the undergraduate academic buildings, the libraries, and the main student residential areas. Its Gothic architecture and ivy-covered walls provide a classic collegiate atmosphere.

Mountaintop Campus

Situated higher up the mountain, this campus is the hub for innovative research and graduate studies. It features facilities like Iacocca Hall and focuses heavily on interdisciplinary collaboration and creative projects.

Murray H. Goodman Campus

Located just a short drive from the main academic areas, this campus is the centre for Lehigh Athletics. It features expansive playing fields, stadiums, and the Stabler Arena, hosting major sporting events and graduation ceremonies.
